Visit note | 2025-09-09 03:00 PM | Dr. Kamrul Hasan, Pulmonology | Patient: Tasnim Miah, 60, female. Mrs. Miah returns for review, reporting persistent wheezing, coughing at night, and a tight chest when exposed to dust or cold air. Her symptoms have been worse since construction dust started near her home in Savar. She works as a shopkeeper and has no other major medical conditions. On examination: SpO2 93%, BP 123/78 mmHg, pulse 92 bpm, weight 52 kg. Chest auscultation reveals widespread expiratory wheezes. Assessment: Bronchial asthma. Plan: a prescription was issued for her maintenance therapy. She was advised to avoid dust and smoke, keep her bedroom well aired, and learn the correct inhaler technique. Follow-up in 1 month to check inhaler technique.

Visit note | 2025-09-09 03:00 PM | Dr. Imran Kabir, Gastroenterology | Patient: Sanjida Bepari, 33, female. Ms. Bepari comes back for follow-up and describes urgency with urgent loose stools every morning with little pain, abdominal bloating, and bowel habits that switch between loose and hard, all of which grow worse under stress. She works as a photographer and notes these complaints have been worse since starting a high-pressure job in Keraniganj. She has no chronic comorbidities. On examination: pain score 3/10, BP 135/71 mmHg, pulse 73 bpm, weight 53 kg. Abdomen is soft with mild tenderness in the left lower quadrant. Assessment: Irritable bowel syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to eat regular meals, keep a food diary, and reduce tea, fizzy drinks, and beans. Follow-up in 6 weeks with the food diary.
